About — Voltic 0 Skip to Content Open Menu Close Menu Open Menu Close Menu Making US-Built Ships Competitive Globally Meet our Team Prosser Cathey - CEO Prosser graduated from MIT in three years, completing three majors. Upon graduation, he won a Fulbright Research Fellowship to study the German auto industry's transition to EVs in Munich. He also rowed for MIT's D1 Heavyweight Crew team, with whom he won a Gold Medal at Head of the Charles. João Seixas de Medeiros João is a Naval Architect and Ocean Engineer with a PhD from MIT and over a decade of experience in hydrodynamics research and vessel design. He has developed advanced software to simulate nonlinear ocean wave behavior, applying it to optimize innovative vessel and wave energy converter designs. His work has earned recognition, including the MIT De Florez award for best graduate design. Yuming Liu Yuming is a senior research faculty member in MIT's Ocean Engineering Department. He has published over 84 times across a range of topics, including design and analysis of ships and marine structures, prediction of ocean environments, and vortical flow dynamics. He earned his PhD in Hydrodynamics from MIT in 1994. Wim van Rees Wim is an associate professor in MIT's Ocean Engineering Department. He has received numerous awards for his research, which focuses on biologically inspired flexible structures for locomotion and renewable energy harvesting. His awards and recognitions include an American Bureau of Shipping Career Development Chair (2017) and a Seagrant Doherty Professorship in Ocean Utilization (2019) Ryan Dooley Ryan has long family tradition in the maritime industry. After attending both the US Merchant Marine Academy and Mass. Maritime Academy he spent 20 years working in operations and sales for shipping lines, port operators, and 3PL’s. He also earned an MBA from Northeastern University and consults for a broad range of maritime decarbonization software providers. Karl McLetchie Karl is a Mechanical and Ocean Engineer with two master's degrees from MIT and more than two decades of design and at-sea experience. Send us your resume at careers@cascade.space . Working at Cascade Space Cascade Space is a young company and our culture and ways of working will evolve as we grow. These are some goals and values we want to foster: Face to face collaboration is important. It's not just about efficiency; we are social creatures and there's only so much information you can communicate over Slack or Zoom. We spend the majority of our working hours together in the office. A heterogenous mix of backgrounds, perspectives, and working styles is critical to our success. We strive to ensure that people are heard and their contributions are valued. We value physical and mental wellbeing. This is a young startup and we work hard, but it's not a continuous fire drill. We have healthy food in the office, take time off to recharge, stay active, and make space to invest in our lives outside of work. Minimizing distractions and context switching is essential to quality and efficient work. There are company wide no-meeting blocks and it's OK to excuse yourself from a meeting if it turns out it's not relevant to you. We also understand that being bolted to a chair from 9 to 6 is not always conducive to effective work; as long as you're getting your work done and effectively communicating/not blocking your coworkers, we're flexible on schedule. If your brain is fried, go for a walk or a bike ride, take a nap, go home — whatever you need to stay engaged. This is a place for learning and growth. We want you to operate just outside of your comfort zone, and want to level people up and have them stick around. It's a small company, but we aim to offer mentorship, regular performance reviews, and consistent equitable leveling. As leaders, we will sometimes fail to live up to our own standards or fail to notice when things are broken. Surfacing problems is never punished, and we own our mistakes, learn from them, and fix them. Psychological safety is essential for healthy and productive teams.
